assignments.node_id: סתימת העינים
assignments.reason: Closing the eyes (סתימת העינים) is the practical method for achieving bitul toward the takhlit. The Torah states explicitly that 'אוֹר הַתַּכְלִית רְחוֹקָה מֵהָאָדָם, וְאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִרְאוֹתוֹ כִּי אִם בִּסְתִימוּ דְּעֵינִין' — one must close one's eyes from the vision of this world to gaze upon the takhlit. Its essential nature is the mechanism of self-nullification: shutting out olam hazeh IS the act of bitul. It belongs with תכלית and בטול as the operational dimension of the same spiritual reality.

assignments.node_id: הסתכלות הזאת
assignments.reason: 'This gazing' (הסתכלות הזאת) refers to the contemplative gaze upon the takhlit — the act of directing one's spiritual vision toward the ultimate purpose where all is one and all is good. It is caused by closing the eyes (edge 916: סתימת העינים → הסתכלות הזאת). Its essential nature is the takhlit-directed vision itself — a direct expression of the bitul/takhlit domain.

assignments.node_id: בטול שנתבטל אל התכלית
assignments.reason: This phrase-node describes the specific act of self-nullification toward the takhlit — 'the bitul whereby one nullified into the takhlit.' It is a variant expression of בטול (already in Package 1) combined with תכלית, placing it squarely in the takhlit/bitul domain. In edge 976, this bitul produces the insight that all suffering is great good.

assignments.node_id: השיג שכל היסורין הם טובות גדולות מאד
assignments.reason: The insight 'he grasped that all sufferings are great goodnesses' is the experiential content of the takhlit-perspective. It IS the realization of כלו טוב (already in Package 1) — when one achieves bitul and gazes at the takhlit, one sees that suffering was always good. Its essential nature is the kulo-tov revelation, not the suffering itself. It is a description of the takhlit-consciousness, not of the suffering domain.

assignments.node_id: הסתכלות על התכלית
assignments.reason: 'Gazing upon the takhlit' (הסתכלות על התכלית) is the core action of Torah #65's central teaching. In edge 2267, this gazing causes all suffering to be nullified. Its essential nature is the directed spiritual vision toward the ultimate purpose — the operational face of the takhlit/bitul cluster. It names the very act that defines Package 1.

assignments.node_id: יוכל להסתכל על התכלית
assignments.reason: 'Can gaze upon the takhlit' — the achieved capacity for takhlit-vision. This is the result-state of focusing one's sight (edges 1273, 1274). Its essential nature is the attainment of the takhlit-perspective, placing it firmly in the bitul/takhlit domain.

assignments.node_id: יוכל להסתכל על התכלית הזה
assignments.reason: Near-identical variant of 'יוכל להסתכל על התכלית' — the capacity to gaze upon this takhlit. Same essential nature: the achieved state of takhlit-directed vision. The added 'הזה' (this) makes no substantive difference to the concept's domain.

assignments.node_id: לסתם את עיניו, ולכון ההסתכלות אל התכלית
assignments.reason: Compound phrase: 'to close his eyes and direct the gaze toward the takhlit.' Combines the method (eye-closing) with its purpose (takhlit-vision). Both components belong to the bitul/takhlit domain. The Torah derives this from the physical analogy of narrowing vision to see something distant — the essential nature is spiritual focusing toward the takhlit.

assignments.node_id: כשרוצים להסתכל על התכלית, שהוא כלו טוב, כלו אחד
assignments.reason: 'When one wants to gaze at the takhlit, which is all-good, all-one.' This phrase-node is the fullest description of the takhlit-gazing act, incorporating both כלו טוב and אחד (both already in Package 1). Its essential nature combines three Package 1 concepts into one statement. Unmistakably in the takhlit/bitul domain.

assignments.node_id: שזוכה אל התכלית
assignments.reason: 'That one merits the takhlit' — the achieved state of arriving at the takhlit-perspective. In edge 2806, this meriting of the takhlit causes the ability to unify all of prayer into 'one' (not passing from one word while already at the next). Its essential nature is the attainment of takhlit-consciousness.

assignments.node_id: בסתימו דעינין. שצריך לסתם את העינים לגמרי, ולסגרם בחזקה מאד, אף גם לדחקם בהאצבע, כדי לסתמם לגמרי
assignments.reason: Extended description of complete eye-closing ('בסתימו דעינין') — sealing the eyes fully, pressing them with the finger, shutting out olam hazeh entirely. This is the most intensive form of סתימת העינים. Its essential nature is the radical withdrawal from this-world's vision as the mechanism for bitul toward the takhlit. The Torah explains this is why people instinctively close their eyes during severe pain — the nefesh knows that takhlit-vision requires complete sealing of worldly sight.

assignments.node_id: צריך לצות ולחבר את הנערים, דהינו הראות, לבלי להסתכל מן הצד על הבלי עולם הזה, לבלתי לנגע את הנפש
assignments.reason: 'One must gather and unite the lads — i.e., the faculty of sight — so as not to look sideways at worldly vanities, so as not to afflict the nefesh.' This describes the focusing of sight as the method for achieving takhlit-vision. Though it mentions the nefesh, its essential nature is the discipline of directing vision — it is the MEANS to bitul/takhlit, not a description of the nefesh's nature. The node describes the operational practice of the takhlit-seeker: concentrating all visual-spiritual energy on the distant light of the takhlit.

assignments.node_id: אפלו כל הצרות והיסורין והרעות העוברין על האדם, חס ושלום, אם יסתכל על התכלית
assignments.reason: 'Even all the troubles and sufferings and evils that pass over a person — if he gazes at the takhlit.' This compound node names the condition (suffering) together with the response (gazing at takhlit). Though it mentions suffering, the essential nature of this node is the takhlit-perspective applied to suffering — it is about what happens WHEN one gazes at the takhlit. The node is a cause-node in an eitza edge whose effect is the revelation that all is good. Its defining character is the takhlit-gaze, not the suffering.

assignments.node_id: בודאי אינם רעות כלל, רק טובות גדולות. כי בודאי כל היסורין באים בכונה מהשם יתברך לטובתו, אם להזכירו שישוב בתשובה, אם למרק עוונותיו. ואם כן היסורין הם טובות גדולות, כי כונת השם יתברך הוא בודאי רק לטובה. נמצא, שבכל הרעות והיסורין שיש לאדם, חס ושלום, אם יסתכל על התכלית, הינו כונת השם יתברך, לא יהיה לו יסורין כלל. רק אדרבא יתמלא שמחה, מגדל רב הטובה שיסתכל בתכלית היסורין הללו
assignments.reason: This long effect-node is the full articulation of the takhlit-revelation: 'certainly they are not evils at all, but great goodnesses...he will be filled with joy from the greatness of the good.' Although it discusses sufferings extensively, its essential nature is the REVELATION that all is good — it IS the כלו טוב experience (Package 1) stated at length. It describes the content of what one sees when one achieves takhlit-perspective: everything is Hashem's good intention. This is the discursive expression of the same reality that Package 1's כלו טוב names in two words.

assignments.node_id: בטול שנתבטל אל התכלית, והשיג שכל היסורין הם טובות גדולות מאד
assignments.reason: Compound phrase combining bitul toward takhlit with the resulting insight about sufferings being great good. This is the fuller variant of 'בטול שנתבטל אל התכלית' (also assigned to Package 1 above). Its essential nature is the bitul-experience and its immediate fruit (the kulo-tov realization) — both core elements of the takhlit/bitul domain. In edge 2972, this compound cause produces שמחה.

assignments.node_id: נתבטלין כל היסורין
assignments.reason: 'All sufferings are nullified' — this describes a state-change of the sufferings themselves. While it is CAUSED by the takhlit-gaze (edge 2267), the node's essential nature is about the sufferings and their transformation. The concept belongs in the suffering domain (Package 4) because it names what happens to the יסורין — they are nullified. It is the effect-side description of what suffering undergoes when the takhlit-perspective is applied. The polarity is neutral (matching Package 4) because suffering-as-a-phenomenon is the domain being described, and its nullification is a state within that domain.

assignments.node_id: שאפלו כשתלך לתבה אחרת, אל תעבר מתבה ראשונה
assignments.reason: 'Even when you go to another word, don't leave the first word' — this describes the unity of prayer-speech, the ability to make all of tefillah into 'one.' In Torah #65, the dibur (speech) emerges from the nefesh (בראשית ב:ז — ויהי האדם לנפש חיה = לרוח ממללא), and each word of prayer pleads with the nefesh not to be abandoned. The essential nature of this node is about the nefesh's speech-prayer-unity — the quality of prayer where the nefesh remains present in every word from beginning to end. This IS the perfected state of the nefesh's speech-capacity, placing it in Package 3 (הנפש — the soul-faculty of speech).

assignments.node_id: כשעיניו מאירות וצופות, בבחינות שדה צופים
assignments.reason: 'When his eyes are illuminated and watchful, in the aspect of שדה צופים (the watchman's field).' This describes the Baal HaSadeh's illuminated state — the condition in which the Field-master can see each soul's distance from the takhlit. Its essential nature is the Field-master's prophetic sight, which is explicitly named as a bechina of שדה צופים (already in the additions for proposed Package 5). The Baal HaSadeh, the שדה, and the watchman-state all belong to the Field/Souls domain.

assignments.node_id: יכול להסתכל בכל אחד ואחד, להביאו אל התכלית. הינו שיכול להסתכל בהדבור של כל אחד, אם אינו על תקונו בשלמות, מחמת שרחוק מהתכלית עדין, אזי הוא מביאו אל התכלית, ואז הדבור כהגן בשלמות
assignments.reason: 'He can look at each and every one, to bring them to the takhlit — he can look at the speech of each one, if it is not yet in its complete repair because they are still distant from the takhlit, and he brings them to the takhlit, and then the speech is complete.' This describes the Baal HaSadeh's function: examining each soul's prayer-speech and guiding it toward the takhlit. While it mentions the takhlit, the essential nature is the Field-master's shepherding activity — the work of the master of the field tending to the souls/trees. This is the defining function of the Baal HaSadeh in proposed Package 5.

assignments.node_id: שכשהנשמות עושין פרות שעושין רצונו של מקום
assignments.reason: 'When the souls bear fruit by doing God's will' — this describes the souls (נשמות) in the Field producing their spiritual fruit. Its essential nature is about the souls/trees of the Field flourishing and fulfilling their purpose. נשמות קדושות is already in the proposed Package 5 additions; this node describes those same souls in their fruitful state. In edge 1682, this soul-fruit causes the Baal HaSadeh's eyes to be illuminated.

assignments.node_id: מאירין עיני בעל השדה, ויכולין להיות צופין ורואין במקום שצריך
assignments.reason: 'The eyes of the Baal HaSadeh are illuminated, and he can be watchful and see where needed.' This describes the illuminated state of the Field-master — his prophetic capacity activated by the souls' good deeds. Its essential nature is the Baal HaSadeh's vision, which is the defining characteristic of the Field/Souls domain. This is the effect-state within the Field ecosystem: when souls bear fruit, the master gains illuminated sight.
